record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: Suppose two local tensors A and B define exactly the same projected entangled pair state on every L × L torus, meaning |Ψ_A⟩ = |Ψ_B⟩ for all system sizes. What local relation between A and B characterizes this equality of PEPS?

evidence.quote: Question 10 What is the relation between two tensors A and B that define the same PEPS, i.e. |ΨA⟩ = |ΨB⟩, on a torus L × L for all possible sizes L?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathbb{C}^d$ (the physical space) and a bond dimension $D$. A translation-invariant projected entangled pair state (PEPS) tensor on the square lattice is a tensor
$$A \in \mathbb{C}^d \otimes (\mathbb{C}^D)^{\otimes 4},$$
with one physical index of dimension $d$ and four virtual indices of dimension $D$ associated with the four nearest-neighbor directions (up, down, left, right). Given a positive integer $L$, the PEPS on the $L\times L$ torus is the vector $|\Psi_A^{(L)}\rangle \in (\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes L^2}$ obtained by placing one copy of $A$ at every site of the $L\times L$ periodic square lattice and contracting matching virtual indices along each edge.

Question. Characterize, in terms of a local algebraic relation between $A$ and $B$, the condition that two such tensors $A,B\in \mathbb{C}^d\otimes(\mathbb{C}^D)^{\otimes 4}$ satisfy
$$|\Psi_A^{(L)}\rangle = |\Psi_B^{(L)}\rangle \qquad \text{for every } L \ge 1.$$
That is, find necessary and sufficient local conditions (e.g., the existence of invertible "gauge" matrices acting on the virtual indices, possibly up to limits) on the pair $(A,B)$ equivalent to producing identical states on every square torus.
artifact.status_search_result: A "fundamental theorem" for PEPS has been established when one requires equality of the states on all contraction geometries: in that setting, two tensors give the same state if and only if they are related by an invertible gauge on the virtual level (up to limits, via minimal canonical forms). However, restricting equality to the family of square tori is known to be substantially harder: deciding whether two tensors generate the same uniform PEPS on all periodic rectangular lattices has been shown to be undecidable (in contrast to the decidable case of all contraction graphs). Thus a clean local characterization for the torus-only case is not known and the original question remains only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: The minimal canonical form of a tensor network
status_evidence.snippet: Two tensors have the same minimal canonical forms iff gauge equivalent up to limits; equivalently they give the same quantum state for any geometry.
status_evidence.claim: A fundamental theorem characterizes equality of tensor network states across all geometries via gauge equivalence (up to limits).

status_evidence.title: Tensor Networks, Fundamental Theorems, and Computational Complexity
status_evidence.snippet: Two PEPS tensors S and T are gauge equivalent iff they contract to the same state on all contraction graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Fundamental theorem holds when equality is required on all contraction graphs.

status_evidence.title: Projected Entangled Pair States: Fundamental Analytical and Numerical Limitations
status_evidence.snippet: Undecidability of deciding whether two tensors generate the same uniform PEPS on periodic rectangular lattices, by reduction to torus tiling.
status_evidence.claim: The torus-only equality problem is undecidable, indicating no simple local characterization is currently known.
